articleSummary: Beijing CDC warns during the May Day holiday to guard against tick bites as ticks emerge with spring warming in northern China. Ticks (hard and soft) can transmit viruses, bacteria, and parasites that cause diseases such as Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), tick-borne encephalitis, and Lyme disease. High-risk activities include outdoor outings in suburbs, mountains, grasslands, and camps; ticks are active in mornings and evenings, with adults peaking April–June and nymphs July–September. Protection tips: avoid tick habitats; wear long sleeves and tucked pants; choose light-colored, smooth fabrics; apply repellents containing DEET or picaridin; use pyrethroid treatments on tents and camping gear. If bitten, remove with pointed tweezers by pulling straight up, disinfect the wound, and preserve the tick for hospital testing; seek medical care if fever or rash develops. Check pets after outings; manage stray cats/dogs to reduce infestations; monitor health after traveling from tick areas.

articleSummary: Neisseria meningitidis meningococcal disease is resurging in Vietnam. From January to March 2026, 24 cases and 4 deaths were reported nationwide, with children under 15 making up 46% of cases. The dual risk is clear: young children are highly susceptible to infection and carriage, while adolescents contribute to transmission in schools, dormitories, and other crowd settings. Most cases present as meningitis (>50%) or fulminant septicemia (5–20%), though pneumonia, conjunctivitis, and other forms occur. Without timely treatment, mortality can reach 50%; even with intervention, 10–15% die and about 20% of survivors have long-term sequelae such as deafness, brain injury, kidney failure, or cognitive impairment. Vaccination is the key preventive measure. Vietnam currently circulates serogroups A, B, C, Y, and W; vaccines protect only specific groups, so full vaccination against multiple serogroups, including B, is recommended for young children, students, and teenagers in crowded settings to curb disease and carriage.

articleSummary: Malaria in Indonesia surpassed 700,000 cases through 2025, up from about 543,000 in prior years, driven by population mobility and weather that affect Anopheles mosquitoes. High-risk groups include people living in or traveling to endemic areas, those near standing water, and individuals active outdoors at night. Remaining challenges are hard-to-reach forest areas and outbreaks in previously malaria-free zones. Strategic steps emphasize epidemiological investigations, migrant surveys, and cross-sector collaboration to achieve 2030 elimination.

articleSummary: Malaria in New Delhi and other malaria-endemic areas is caused by Plasmodium via Anopheles mosquitoes; dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes and can occur wherever mosquitoes exist. articleHeadlineTranslated: A Wake-Up Call About Rabies in Tay Ninh
articleHeadline: Hồi chuông cảnh báo bệnh dại ở Tây Ninh
articleSummary: Rabies in Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam, saw 7 deaths and 4 animal outbreaks in the first three months of 2026. All fatalities occurred in individuals who did not receive post-exposure vaccination or rabies immunoglobulin after dog or cat bites, with many patients using unsafe folk remedies for wound care. The province houses more than 198,000 dogs and cats across over 100,000 households, but vaccination coverage is only about 34.4%, well below the 70% herd-immunity target. Roaming pets and limited containment heighten human exposure, especially in rural areas. Local authorities have implemented integrated measures: surveillance, exposure lists, vaccination counseling, veterinary containment of outbreaks, and intensified public communication. WHO guidance underscores 70% pet vaccination to block transmission; gaps persist in smallholder and roaming settings. Public guidance emphasizes immediate wound washing for 15 minutes, prompt medical care for vaccination or immunoglobulin, and avoiding folk remedies; owners should vaccinate and restrain pets. In Ho Chi Minh City, 3 rabies deaths were reported by April 20, 2026.
notes: ターイニン省ではヤギ予防接種率が34.4%と世界的な集団免疫目標70%を大きく下回り、未治療の犬猫咬傷と民間療法の使用が致命的転帰につながっている。ホーチミン市でも3例の死亡が報告され、複数の都市での多発事例を示唆している。局所当局による統合的対策が報告されているが、実施の有効性はまだ評価段階。

articleSummary: Seasonal influenza, not just a cold, causes acute respiratory illness from influenza A and B viruses. As of May 3, 2026, China CDC warns we are in peak flu season. Globally, WHO estimates about 1 billion infections annually, 3–5 million severe cases, and 290k–650k deaths. Symptoms include high fever over 39°C, severe headaches and myalgias, persistent cough, and marked fatigue; severe cases may progress to pneumonia, myocarditis, or ARDS. Reasons for winter surge include colder, drier air, crowded indoor settings, waning immunity, and frequent viral mutations reducing vaccine effectiveness. Misconceptions: vaccines don’t guarantee protection; fever alone doesn’t confirm flu; prior infection doesn’t ensure immunity; masks aren’t necessary. Prevention emphasizes annual vaccination in autumn (Sept–Nov), mask use in crowds, strict hand hygiene, and healthy living to bolster immunity, with early care if symptoms arise. Distinguishing influenza A from other infections requires testing.

articleHeadline: Mengenal Virus Campak, Hasil Evolusi Rinderpest yang Menyerang Sapi
articleSummary: Indonesia reported 63,769 suspected measles cases in 2025, with 11,094 laboratory-confirmed and 69 deaths. By week 7 of 2026, the Health Ministry records 8,224 suspected cases, 572 confirmed, and 4 deaths, plus 21 suspected measles outbreaks and 13 laboratory-confirmed outbreaks across 17 districts/cities in 11 provinces. Measles is an enveloped, single-stranded, negative-sense RNA Morbillivirus in the Paramyxoviridae family; humans are the only natural hosts. The virus is believed to have evolved from Rinderpest, a cattle pathogen, with spillover to humans around the 6th century BCE. Koplik spots in the oral mucosa can appear about 2 days before rash and aid early diagnosis; prevalence 60–70% among patients. Incubation 10–14 days; rash is morbilliform, starting on the face/neck and spreading downward, lasting 3–7 days. Measles is highly contagious, spreading from 4 days before to 4 days after rash; a single case can generate up to 18 secondary infections.

articleHeadline: Climate and socioeconomic factors drive heterogeneous dengue risk escalation in the Chinese population - Communications Medicine
articleSummary: Dengue risk in China is increasingly shaped by climate change and rapid urbanization. Using a geographically explainable AI (GeoXAI) model, the study estimates dengue hazard for 2024 (current), 2050, and 2100 under three SSP scenarios, integrating hazard, exposure, and vulnerability into a hazard-exposure-vulnerability framework. A northward expansion of high-hazard areas is detected, with the coldest-month minimum temperature as the dominant driver (27.2% contribution), while socioeconomic factors such as population density (3.8%) and urbanization level (2.7%) further amplify hazard. Present high-risk clusters lie in Southwest China and megacities; future risk shows spatially heterogeneous escalation, with Southwest and Southeast China bearing the steepest growth, and Northwest China showing disproportionate increases. Under SSP585, dengue risk increases by 6.01% in 2050 and 8.21% in 2100—the largest rise among the three SSPs. The authors call for intensified integrated surveillance and multidimensional interventions, with implications for other Aedes-borne diseases like chikungunya.

articleSummary: Gruinard Island, a small northwest Scottish island nicknamed 'Anthrax Island', was used during World War II by the British government for biological weapons tests. The bodies of animals used in experiments were dumped there. The anthrax-causing Bacillus anthracis bacterium was studied on this site, leaving Gruinard heavily contaminated for about five decades. By the late 1990s scientists decontaminated the island, but it remains abandoned. Bacillus anthracis is described as an extremely deadly Category A agent with high transmission potential and mortality, with routes of spread including dust, food, and water. It is alleged that Japan used anthrax against China during the war. In 2001, spores in powder form were mailed through the U.S. Postal Service, affecting 22 people and killing 5. Nearby North Sentinel Island in the Indian Ocean, part of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands, is largely isolated and off-limits.
